# GitHub Evidence Checklist: Agentic Software Engineering System: URL Shortener

**Purpose**: Validate that repository contents, history, and committed evidence are defined for reviewers
**Created**: 2026-10-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.
**Legend**: `[M]` mandatory (a constitution MUST, an approved requirement, or an approved decision); `[O]` optional enhancement or backlog boundary. `G0` is evaluable now against the approved specification, plan, ADRs, and contracts; `G1` is evaluable after `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-analyze`, before implementation. `{Detects: ...}` links an item to a failure pattern in the [README](README.md) detection matrix. Dimension tags: Completeness, Clarity, Consistency, Measurability, Coverage, Traceability, Edge Case, Assumption, Conflict, Gap.
## Contents and Layout

- [ ] CHK001 - Are the repository contents a reviewer must find defined (spec, plan, ADRs, contracts, tasks, code, tests, evidence, final report) with locations? [Completeness, Spec DEC-100, DEC-111] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the evidence directory layout defined (scenario-a, scenario-b, scenario-c, verify, traces, final-report.md) consistently across plan, ADRs, and quickstart? [Consistency, Spec DEC-100, DEC-111] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK003 - Is a reviewer entry point defined? [Gap, Constitution X] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK004 - Is the retention rule defined (kept for the assessment, no size limit) and consistent with audit retention? [Consistency, Spec DEC-112, ASM-016] [M, G0]

## History and Provenance

- [ ] CHK005 - Are commits required to be small and logically coherent with messages stating engineering intent, with a checking rule? [Measurability, Constitution X, POL-TRC-005] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK006 - Must the test commit precede the implementing commit so red-before-green is visible in history? [Coverage, Testing §1, Constitution IV] [M, G0] {Detects: implementation-before-spec-or-tests}
- [ ] CHK007 - Are commit ranges required to show which work was orchestrator-run and which was not? [Clarity, ADR-013] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is history rewriting (force push, rebase of published evidence) prohibited or defined as destructive and gated? [Gap, Orchestration G-DESTR] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the merge rule defined (feature branch, no automatic merge to main, human merges)? [Coverage, Spec FR-133 NAC] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK010 - Is the branch used for the work and its final pushed state defined for reviewers? [Gap, Plan §5] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK011 - Is a pull-request or review process defined, or explicitly excluded? [Gap, Constitution X] [O, G0]

## Evidence Integrity

- [ ] CHK012 - Must evidence files be generated (not hand-edited) and carry hashes so alteration is detectable? [Coverage, Observability §7] [M, G0] {Detects: fabricated-results}
- [ ] CHK013 - Must every committed evidence item carry agent_mode, clock_kind, synthetic, or OFFLINE labels? [Completeness, Observability §7, Spec DEC-044] [M, G0] {Detects: fabricated-results}
- [ ] CHK014 - Are illustrative files excluded from evidence by rule? [Coverage, Contracts README] [M, G0] {Detects: fabricated-results}
- [ ] CHK015 - Are prohibited commit contents defined (secrets, .secrets, database dumps, raw addresses) with a secret-scan detection over evidence? [Completeness, Spec DEC-112, Security §4.3] [M, G0]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the absence of CI stated, with committed local verify output as the substitute evidence? [Clarity, Spec DEC-099] [M, G0] {Detects: unsupported-completion-claims}

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items marked `[Gap]` or `[Conflict]` name a place where the current documents are silent or disagree; they are findings for the reviewer to resolve, not pre-judged results
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially within this file (`CHK001` onward); cite them as `<file>:CHKnnn`
